Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testNewStringNullInput_CODEC229()` expects that calling `StringUtils.newStringUtf8(null)` and `StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(null)` returns `null`. The test fails because `newStringIso8859_1(null)` throws a NullPointerException (NPE) instead of returning `null`, indicating inconsistent handling of `null` input between these two methods.

Inspecting the code shows:
- `StringUtils.newStringUtf8(byte[] bytes)` simply delegates to `newString(bytes, Charsets.UTF_8)`.
- The private method `newString(byte[] bytes, Charset charset)` correctly handles `null` bytes by returning `null`:
  ```java
  return bytes == null ? null : new String(bytes, charset);
  ```
- However, `StringUtils.newStringIso8859_1(byte[] bytes)` directly calls `new String(bytes, Charsets.ISO_8859_1)` without any null check.

This direct call to the `String` constructor with a `null` byte array causes the NPE. Previously, it might have delegated to the private method `newString` which had the null check. The bug report mentions that the null-handling capability was lost after a refactor tied to the fix for CODEC-136 (switching to Charset objects). Hence, `newStringIso8859_1` no longer protects against null inputs, unlike `newStringUtf8`.

In summary, inconsistent handling of null inputs is due to `newStringIso8859_1` bypassing the null-safe `newString` method, leading to NullPointerException when passing null bytes. The correct behavior is demonstrated in `newStringUtf8` which delegates to the null-safe method. This explains why the test expecting null return fails with NPE.

Suggested fix: modify `newStringIso8859_1` to delegate to the null-safe `newString` method like `newStringUtf8` does.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
